policy.name: Supreme Court ends tariffs under IEEPA (Learning Resources v. Trump)
policy.value: The emergency-powers (IEEPA) tariffs, including the 2025 reciprocal tariffs, were held unlawful. Tariffs under other laws (Section 301, Section 232) were not affected.
policy.quote: Held: IEEPA does not authorize the President to impose tariffs.
policy.publisher: Supreme Court of the United States, slip opinion No. 24-1287

policy.name: Section 122 import surcharge (temporary bridge)
policy.status: in effect 2026-02-24 to 2026-07-24, then expired at its 150-day limit
policy.quote: shall continue in effect through 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 24, 2026
policy.publisher: White House proclamation, Imposing a Temporary Import Surcharge

policy.name: New Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies (forced labor investigations), replacing the Section 122 surcharge
policy.value: China is in the 12.5% tier. Lithium-ion batteries (HTS 8507.60) are not on the general exemption list, and the notice says these duties apply on top of other duties in the same subchapter, which also holds the older China Section 301 duties (our reading). So Chinese LFP cells and packs pay 12.5% plus the 25% China Section 301 rate plus the normal duty.
policy.quote: the Trade Representative has determined to impose 12.5 percent tariffs on products of China
policy.quote_more: shall also be subject to any additional duty provided for in this subchapter
policy.publisher: USTR, Notice of Actions in the forced labor Section 301 investigations (Federal Register doc. 2026-15181, published 2026-07-28)

policy.name: IRS Notice 2026-15 (primary): foreign-content test for the storage tax credit
policy.status: issued; applies to storage that begins construction after 2025-12-31
policy.value: For storage that begins construction in 2026, at least 55% of its direct costs must come from outside prohibited foreign entities (the material assistance cost ratio), or the 48E credit is lost. The law raises the bar to 60% for 2027, 65% for 2028, 70% for 2029 and 75% after 2029.
policy.quote: in the case of an EST which begins construction during calendar year 2026, the Clean Electricity MACR cannot be less than 55%.

policy.name: AD/CVD on Chinese active anode material (graphite)
policy.status: NOT imposed. Commerce found rates near 160-170% but the ITC voted negative on 2026-03-12.
policy.quote: Therefore, neither the anti-dumping duties (AD) nor the countervailing duties (CVD) took effect.

alternatives.quote: MacMic is planning a 10% increase in IGBT (Insulated-Gate Bipolar Transistor) prices

parts.risk_note: Power semiconductors are on 30 to 52 week lead times with three rounds of 2026 price hikes, so inverter builds need parts ordered most of a year ahead.

our_read.label: Long wait
our_read.why: Order most of a year ahead. Power chips are the longest lead item inside the box.

parts.name: Memory in the battery controller and gateway (MCU flash, DRAM, eMMC/NAND)
parts.what_it_does: The battery management microcontrollers keep their firmware in on-chip flash. A gateway that runs Linux (app, fleet dispatch, over-the-air updates) pairs an applications processor with separate DRAM (DDR4 or LPDDR4) and eMMC flash for the operating system, firmware images and logs. The cellular modem carries its own memory. Base has not published its parts; the list below shows typical parts for this class of device.

lead_time.value: 32-40+ weeks for standard DDR4 and DDR5 modules in some cases, under allocation
lead_time.quote: Lead times on standard DDR4 and DDR5 modules have already stretched to 32–40+ weeks in some cases
lead_time.source_quality: vendor blog, not an independent survey

price_trend.value: Conventional DRAM contract prices +45-50% QoQ in 4Q25, forecast +90-95% QoQ in 1Q26, +13-18% in 3Q26, +10-15% in 4Q26. NAND +15-20% in 4Q26. DDR4 heads to record per-gigabit prices in 2026 as supply drops; 64Gb MLC NAND spot prices more than tripled from end-2025.
price_trend.quote: Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 45-50% QoQ

more.quote: with conventional DRAM prices expected to surge 90-95% QoQ
Conventional DRAM contract prices are forecast to rise 13-18% QoQ in 3Q26
Conventional DRAM contract prices are projected to grow 10–15% QoQ in 4Q26, while NAND Flash contract prices are expected to increase 15–20%
July consumer DDR4 contract prices have already risen by more than 60-85%.
We believe that the aggregate industry supply will remain substantially short of the demand for the foreseeable future.
more.publisher: The Register, quoting Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra

more.quote: DDR4 supply is set to drop sharply in 2026, pushing per-gigabit prices to record highs.
64Gb MLC NAND spot prices have surged more than 300% from end-2025 levels

price_trend.conflict: TrendForce News (2026-10-20), citing Commercial Times, reported 4Q26 DRAM contract prices rising about 20% QoQ. TrendForce's own press release (2026-09-30) says 10-15% for conventional DRAM; the page uses the press release.

concentration.value: Allocation goes to AI and server first; industrial and consumer DDR4 users rank last
concentration.quote: Memory suppliers continue to prioritize capacity allocation toward higher-margin AI and server products

more.quote: ranks behind PC and server applications in suppliers' allocation priorities.

concentration.share_note: DRAM is made mainly by Samsung, SK hynix and Micron; no dated share quote collected (not found in this pass).

policy.name: Section 301 on Chinese-origin semiconductors
policy.publisher: USTR, Notice of Modification (Federal Register doc. 2024-21217)

policy.name: New Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies (forced labor investigations)
policy.value: Does not apply to memory chips: HTS 8542.32 (memories) and other 8542 integrated circuits are on the general exemption list.
policy.quote: shall not apply to articles that are classifiable in the following provisions of the HTSUS
policy.publisher: USTR, Notice of Actions in the forced labor Section 301 investigations (Federal Register doc. 2026-15181, published 2026-07-28)

alternatives.name: Winbond, Nanya and other Taiwanese DDR4 makers
alternatives.note: Still producing DDR4 as Micron, Samsung and SK hynix exit; TrendForce says their expansion cannot fully offset the cut.

alternatives.name: Design out discrete DRAM
alternatives.note: MCUs with on-chip SRAM and flash avoid buying commodity DRAM at all.

parts.risk_note: Memory is a small share of the bill, but the parts a controller and gateway use (DDR4, LPDDR4, low-capacity NAND) are the ones the three biggest makers are retiring in 2025-2026, while prices hit records and supply goes to AI servers first. The risk is a gateway line stopping for one missing chip, or a forced board redesign when a part goes end of life.

our_read.label: Allocation and end of life
our_read.why: Cheap per unit but not safe: the legacy DDR4, LPDDR4 and NAND these boards use are being retired by the biggest makers. Plan last-time buys, second sources and long-life parts now.

memory_parts.note: Firmware and working memory sit inside the microcontroller, so no separate memory chip is bought. Example: NXP S32K146, the microcontroller in an NXP battery management reference design.
memory_parts.quote: 1 MB Flash, 128 K static random-access memory (SRAM)

memory_parts.part: DRAM for a Linux gateway (DDR4, LPDDR4, DDR3L)
memory_parts.note: An applications processor needs external DRAM. Example: NXP i.MX 8M Mini, an industrial IoT processor.
memory_parts.quote: The DRAM controller supports 32-bit/16-bit LPDDR4, DDR4, and DDR3L memory.
memory_parts.publisher: NXP, i.MX 8M Mini industrial datasheet, Rev. 2

memory_parts.part: eMMC or raw NAND for the operating system, firmware and logs
memory_parts.note: The same processor boots and stores data from eMMC or raw SLC/MLC NAND.
memory_parts.quote: eMMC 5.1 Flash (2 interfaces, uSDHC1 and uSDHC3)
memory_parts.publisher: NXP, i.MX 8M Mini industrial datasheet, Rev. 2

memory_parts.note: Module makers pass memory costs through. Berg Insight found price pressure rather than shortages, with 4G LTE modules on legacy memory less exposed than 5G.
memory_parts.quote: The most immediate impact on the module market revealed in the report has been price pressure rather than shortages

eol.value: End-of-life notices sent to PC and data center customers in 2025. Micron reportedly keeps supplying long-term automotive, industrial and networking customers.
eol.quote: Micron will reportedly continue supplying DDR4 and LPDDR4 memory to long-term customers in the automotive, industrial, and networking sectors

eol.value: Sticking to its DDR4 end-of-life plan despite high prices.
eol.quote: TrendForce notes that Samsung is sticking firmly to its end-of-life plan.

eol.value: Plans to phase DDR4 out by 2026; converted its Wuxi fab to a newer node.
eol.quote: Like Samsung, SK hynix has signaled plans to phase out DDR4 by 2026.

eol.value: Samsung's last MLC NAND shipments were due June 2026; world MLC NAND capacity forecast down 41.7% in 2026. Demand comes mostly from industrial control, automotive, medical and networking.
eol.quote: the worldwide MLC NAND Flash capacity is expected to decrease by 41.7% YOY in 2026

eol.who: Kioxia, 2D (floating-gate) NAND and BiCS FLASH gen 3
eol.value: End-of-life notice of 2026-03-31: final orders by end of September 2026, last shipments by December 2028.
eol.quote: the company plans to take final orders by end-September this year, complete last shipments by December 2028

eol.value: Counter-trend: Micron started 1-alpha DRAM in Manassas for long-lifecycle DDR4 and LPDDR4, will quadruple DDR4 wafer supply there, and expects qualified output by end of 2026.
eol.quote: Micron expects qualified 1α DRAM production from the Manassas fab by the end of calendar year 2026.

mitigations.name: Last-time buy inside the final-order window
mitigations.note: End-of-life notices give a fixed last order date. Buy enough DDR4, LPDDR4 or NAND for the product's remaining builds and spares before it closes; for Kioxia 2D NAND that date was end of September 2026.

mitigations.name: Design in parts with a written longevity commitment
mitigations.note: Processors and microcontrollers in NXP's longevity program are guaranteed for 10 to 15 years from launch; ST commits 10 years for STM32, renewed each year; Micron says Manassas will make long-lifecycle DDR4 and LPDDR4.
mitigations.quote: guaranteed product availability for a minimum of 10 to 15 years from the product’s launch date

more.quote: ST’s product longevity program ensures a long-term availability of 10 years for STM32 microcontrollers, with a commitment renewed annually.

mitigations.name: Qualify a second memory source
mitigations.note: Processor makers publish lists of DRAM parts validated on their chips. Qualify parts from two makers (for DDR4, Winbond or Nanya as well as Micron) so one allocation cut does not stop the line.
mitigations.quote: They also include a list of NXP and vendor-validated memory part numbers.

mitigations.name: Commit volumes early
mitigations.note: Open-market memory is sold under allocation, and buyers expect DRAM to stay tight in 2027. Agreed quarterly volumes get served first.
mitigations.quote: PC OEMs continue to procure aggressively amid expectations that DRAM supply will remain tight in 2027

mitigations.name: Keep discrete memory off the battery controller
mitigations.note: Battery management on a microcontroller with on-chip flash and SRAM needs no DRAM; keep the Linux gateway as the only board that does.

about: One home battery, part by part: how long each part takes to get, where prices are heading, where it comes from, and which 2026 US rules touch it. Every number links to a dated public source. "Our read" is this site's judgment, not a source. Independent, not affiliated with Base Power.
